Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

agent noun

someone who acts or does business for another

also agents, representative, sales agent, act through an agent

classical

Cic. Caecin. 57: aliēnī jūris vicārius
Traupman 169, 219: itinerum prōcūrātor, travel agent

prōcūrātor, prōcūrātōris m.

noun, third declension

an agent, someone who manages affairs for another

Also a manager (see manager); Traupman forms modern agents with it, as itinerum prōcūrātor, travel agent.

Other words

  • īnstitor, īnstitōris m. — one who sells goods for another; a hawker

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 22.25.19: ipsum īnstitōrem mercis; Hor. Epod. 17.20 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • is quī lēgitimē prōcūrātor dīcitur, omnium rērum ejus quī in Ītaliā nōn sit absitve reī pūblicae causā quasi quīdam paene dominus, hoc est aliēnī jūris vicārius

    the man who is properly called an agent: for someone who is not in Italy, or is away on public business, he is almost a kind of owner of everything, that is, a deputy for another’s rightsCic. Caecin. 57

See also manager, travel agent, ticket agent, represent, agent.

SourcesLewis & Short: procurator · Lewis & Short: institor
